(the manufacturing plant in Yamanashi). These are genuinely different legal entities within the same group.

The rules say: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

The document page shows "Endress+Hauser Yamanash..." which is the truncated form of "Yamanashi". So the "document" value "Endress+Hauser Yamanashi Co., Ltd." presumably comes from the actual certificate page text (truncated "Yamanash" in the excerpt, but presumably complete in the full extraction).

So verdict: different-entity. Best value: document's — "Endress+Hauser Yamanashi Co., Ltd."

Why: The certificate names Endress+Hauser Yamanashi Co., Ltd., which is a distinct legal entity from Endress+Hauser Japan Co., Ltd., not mere spelling drift; since the certificate is the legal instrument, carry the document's value.
